body.statement: Shu--Wang--Li, Theorem 2, gives for their scalar \(\operatorname{PNS}(k)\) the lower pieces \(0\), \(\sum_ja_j-k+1\), and \(b_i+\sum_{j\ne i}(a_j+p_j-b_j)-k+1\), and the upper pieces \(\sum_{j\leq k}b_j+\sum_{j>k}p_j\), the margins \(a_j\), and \(\sum_{j\in S}(a_j-b_j)/(|S|-1)\) for \(|S|\geq2\).  Their Theorems 6 and 7 respectively give zero-probability padding for unequal finite alphabets and replacement of queried outcome labels.

attestation.note: Verified directly against Theorem 2 (displayed scalar pieces), Theorem 6 (unequal-alphabet padding), and Theorem 7 (label replacement) in the cited version; no general-tightness claim is attributed to the source.

body.justification: This cited leaf carries only the published formula and relabeling attribution used by the sharpness theorem.
body.gap: The cited paper proves soundness but states that general-dimensional tightness remains open; attainment is proved separately here.
body.consumer: The algebraic comparison identifies the newly attained interval with the published scalar bounds.
